name: Adolf Eichmann
role: SS-Obersturmbannführer; head of RSHA Referat IV B4 (Jewish affairs and deportations), executed 1962
summary: Eichmann was a long-standing National Socialist and SS officer who organised forced Jewish emigration and then the deportation of Jews to the killing sites. He described himself at trial as bound by oath and orders; in the 1957 Sassen interviews, as quoted in published sources, he spoke of the Jews as an enemy and of having no regrets. Only the positions his own record and statements document are recorded here; most statements are left unanswered.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: His testimony describes his Vienna and Berlin offices financing and organising forced emigration of Jews; this is a thin match for the statement, so low.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His record is organising the expulsion and deportation to killing centres of Jews, treating them as a group without equal claim to rights or life.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His record is organising the forced emigration and deportation of Jews from Germany and German-occupied Europe, a policy of building a national community by removing a group defined by descent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He did not deny the Holocaust: his record is organising the deportation of over 1.5 million Jews to killing centres and sites, and preparing the presentation for the Wannsee Conference.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: In a 1957 manuscript he wrote that Jewry throughout the world had 'evidently declared war' on Germany through Chaim Weizmann; at trial he said this described events of the period and did not refer to the Jews' acts as such. This is an open-war claim rather than a secret plot, so it is recorded as contested.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He stated at trial that he tried to live by the Kantian imperative as he understood it and that he carried out orders under his oath; he held that obedience to the state's orders and laws was a duty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He agreed at trial that an oath was one of the highest moral obligations and that he was bound by oaths of loyalty to Hitler and to Himmler; he knew the party was built on the Fuehrer principle.

population-transfer.rationale: His record is the forced removal of a minority: coerced emigration from Vienna (1938), the Nisko deportations and the deportation of Jews across Europe from RSHA IV B4.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He ran the offices that forced people classified as Jews out of the Reich and then deported over a million of them, carrying out the racial policy in administrative practice.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: His record is the forced removal of Jews from Germany and German-held Europe: coerced emigration from Vienna, the Nisko deportations and the later deportations, all driven by his offices.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He described himself (in the Sassen text read at trial) as one of those who carried out orders without reserve in accordance with his oath, and testified that one could not refuse during the war.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He argued that he acted lawfully under the Reich's orders and laws and that his oath bound him; he did not claim any order or law lost its force because it was unjust.

notes: His accounts conflict: at the 1961 trial he said he had no hatred of Jews, never thought annihilation justified and acted on orders, while the 1957 Sassen material (secondhand, via the Jewish Virtual Library and Wikipedia) records him as unrepentant. The trial court found he believed in the Nazi cause. Answers weigh his record of measures he personally drove, and mark contested points low. The interrogation was read into the trial record (see notFound for the prison memoirs and the Less interrogation volume). Themes searched in the later pass: means, world, society and liberty, for the statements added since the first pass; only forced removal of a minority was documented by his record, the rest stay null.
